title: Suraksha Diagnostic Ltd - 544293 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Suraksha Diagnostic Q1 FY27 total income rose 21% YoY to INR 887 million, with PAT up 40% to INR 128 million and EBITDA margin at 36%.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 21% YoY to INR 887 million and EBITDA rose 28% to INR 315 million, with margin expanding about 200 bps to 36%. PAT grew 40% to INR 128 million (14.7% margin). The network reached 72 centres after one hub and three spokes were added in Q1, with three more hubs/spokes opened in July-August and a hub commissioned in Jharkhand. Management reiterated 100 centres by FY28 and guided EBITDA margin of at least 34% for FY27. Analysts pressed on the slowdown in test volume growth (about 10-11% vs ~20% in prior two quarters), repeat-patient decline, and the conservative 15% revenue guidance.

financial_highlights.change: from -5.5% last quarter; first profitable quarter
+136% YoY; fifth consecutive quarter of sequential growth

segments.name: Mature centres (>2 years, ~42-45 centres)
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 12-12.5% YoY (management cited QoQ and YoY figures interchangeably); EBITDA margin 40.9%, attributed to volume, genomics contribution and lower COGS after biochemistry shift from Siemens to Roche.

segments.name: Centres under 2 years (27 centres)
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR 85 million (Rs 8.5 crore) of INR 880 million quarterly sales per management; turned EBITDA positive at 6.5%.

segments.name: Genomics
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 13.7 million (+136% YoY); mix 80% B2C and 20% B2B; genomic margins estimated at 15-20%; Rs 22 crore invested over three years.

segments.name: Wellness / corporate
segments.commentary: Wellness contribution about 4-5% of revenue; CGHS rate revision from mid-October 2025 added about 1.5% to top line per management, with public-sector corporate contributing around 15%.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin to be not below 34% for FY27; management expects more by FY29 (analyst cited 33-34% by FY28-29).
Q2 expected strong (seasonal disease season), Q3 muted (festivities and winter), Q4 strong; July-August trends described as robust.
Genomics growth expected at about 20% per quarter through FY27.
Capex of about Rs 70-80 crore in FY27; on track for 100 centres by FY28.
Plan to add 4 hubs and 7 spokes for the rest of FY27 (corrected from 3 hubs and 6 spokes after clarification, with 3 hubs and 6 spokes stated in one answer).
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27: one hub and three spoke centres commissioned; July-August added two hubs and three spokes; network at 72 centres at quarter end.
Hub capex about Rs 10-10.5 crore; spoke capex about Rs 1.5-2 crore; spoke centre-level breakeven 3-4 months, HO-level breakeven 8-9 months.
Genexus rapid genome sequencer acquired, in final validation; turnaround for oncology genomic study cut from 14-17 days to 48 hours.
No major additional genomics capex expected in next 2-3 years per CSO.

Kolkata proper: 5 hubs and 6 spokes, with room for 3 more hubs and at least 6 spokes; Greater Kolkata has 9 hubs with scope to double. Jharkhand hub commissioned, another planned with 5 spokes; Assam hub operating with spoke commissioned and another under construction; Agartala (Tripura) hub to follow.
demand_pricing: Like-for-like mature centre revenue growth about 12% YoY; test volume growth about 10-11%; growth attributed to test mix change, with no price increases taken per management.
Patient footfall for consultation up about 11% YoY in June 2026; patient volume up 12.4% QoQ per management.
Repeat patient share down to about 40% (from 52% in FY22-23), which management attributed to new patient additions from expansion, not absolute decline.
B2B carries a margin challenge but volume offsets it; B2C seen as margin-stable with no deep discounting.
Franchisee-run collection centres number 214; these are used as feeder points before spokes are opened.
Organised share of diagnostics in East India is lower than the national 15-20%; Suraksha claimed to be the largest organised player in the region.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the ~400 bps margin expansion and can margins reach 33-34% by FY28-29?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating leverage as revenue scales against largely fixed costs; management said it expects margins to be higher than 33-34% by FY29 and that mature-centre margins are sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 EBITDA margin outlook given the seasonal pattern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said overall EBITDA will not go below 34% for the year, with Q2 and Q4 strong and Q3 muted.

qa_highlights.question: Why has test volume growth slowed to about 10-11% from around 20% in prior quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was nothing specific and that the company would evaluate it; it did not give a reason.

qa_highlights.question: What is the genomics market size and B2B/B2C split?
qa_highlights.answer: Split is 80% B2C and 20% B2B, with B2B expected to grow as a share. Indian genomics market cited at about Rs 450 million by 2030 (figure as stated; unit unclear). Average realisation not given, since genomic test prices range from Rs 4,000-5,000 to over Rs 50,000.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ROCE/ROE below national peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to the young centre base (27 of 45 mature centres under 2 years old); lower only against three or four players.

qa_highlights.question: Are franchisee collection centres affected by new spokes?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; when a collection centre area proves strong, a spoke is opened and the franchisee is relocated to a further location.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 revenue guidance only 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: CSO said the company has been conservative as it is a relatively new organisation; no dearth of effort.

risks_watch: Test volume growth slowed to about 10-11% YoY from about 20% in prior two quarters; management said only that it would evaluate the reason, with no explanation given.
Repeat patient share fell to about 40% from 52% in FY22-23; management attributes this to new-patient additions, not absolute decline, so track absolute repeat volumes next quarter.

Margin trajectory depends on 27 of 45 mature centres being under 2 years old; management flagged likely dilution from new centre additions even as the 6.5% margin on younger centres is expected to rise.
Mature-centre revenue growth of about 12% YoY is the like-for-like base; cannibalisation from spoke openings was acknowledged but not quantified.
Genomics revenue remains small (INR 13.7 million); average realisation not disclosed and the Rs 22 crore investment has no stated payback or revenue target beyond ~20% quarterly growth.
Expansion plan of 4 hubs and 7 spokes for the rest of FY27 was stated inconsistently during Q&A (3 hubs and 6 spokes in one answer); confirm the final count against the presentation.
Revenue guidance of 15% for FY27 was described as conservative; watch whether actual growth exceeds it.
Capex of Rs 70-80 crore for FY27 and the 100-centre target by FY28 require sustained hub and spoke openings in new states such as Jharkhand, Assam and Tripura.
key_quotes: So, we believe that the EBITDA, overall EBITDA will not go below 34%.
No, it is due to the mix change. We have not increased any prices.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on margins, genomics and the expansion roadmap, repeatedly citing "very strong" and "robust" trends. It was noticeably evasive on test volume deceleration, answering "nothing very specific" and "we will evaluate that," and on the reasons for the conservative 15% revenue guidance it cited being a new organisation.

growth.why: Management guides 15% revenue growth and EBITDA margin of at least 34% for FY27, backed by a specific build-out (6 spokes and 3 hubs more in FY27, Rs 70-80 crore capex, 100 centres by FY28) and genomics growth of ~20% a quarter, though test volume growth has slowed to ~10-11% and the 15% revenue guide is not explicitly tied to order or price numbers.
